expectations.text: Recommends keeping calculatePrice as its own file (rejects inlining it into the component)
expectations.evidence: Title 'Don't inline it. Keep `calculatePrice.ts` as is.' and recommendation: 'Keep `pricing/calculatePrice.ts` and its test exactly where they are.'

expectations.text: Grounds it in the abstraction-over-file-structure heuristic (clean typed interface, hides implementation)
expectations.evidence: 'That's a real abstraction... It has an interface, it hides its implementation, and it reduces the context needed on both sides of the boundary. That's the single most valuable property you can have in an AI-assisted codebase.'

expectations.text: Notes the agent uses the typed call site without needing the internals (understood in isolation)
expectations.evidence: 'An agent editing CheckoutSummary reads calculatePrice(input): Price at the call site and knows everything it needs to proceed without opening the file.' and 'Understandable in isolation.'

expectations.text: Rejects the 'inline so Claude sees it all' argument for a clean, reused, tested abstraction
expectations.evidence: Directly rebuts the teammate: 'it's solving a problem that calculatePrice.ts doesn't actually have' and 'agents follow a single explicit import far more reliably than they reconstruct logic buried in a 300-line component.'
